current_evidence: The council's 'Planning application forms' download page (download/273) lists 'Validation checklist' as file 3598, with no newer validation document. A hull.gov.uk search found no replacement list or consultation, and the document text states it was adopted on 17 January 2023.

issues.detail: List date is recorded as 2023-01-01, but the text Grokbot cites says the list was 'Adopted 17th January, 2023'. The date should be 2023-01-17.

Grokbot has no row for these local items, each with its own trigger in the source: existing and proposed site/block plan at 1:100 or 1:200 (new buildings or layout changes); site sections, finished floor and site levels (changes in site levels); window details at 1:20 (all new or replacement windows); car parking layout (new parking or vehicle access); viability assessment (arguments for reduced provision, or heritage harm justified on viability); open space assessment (development on or loss of open space, sports or recreation land); sports pitch statement (loss of or building on sports pitches); visual amenity/townscape assessment (buildings over 30m, or bordering open countryside); drainage plans (new buildings needing new surface or foul drainage); hydrogeological risk assessment (within groundwater Source Protection Zones); air quality assessment (residential in the AQMA, Local Plan map 13.1, or development within 200m of the Humber Estuary SAC); lighting impact assessment (light affecting people or wildlife); daylight/sunlight assessment (new residential where daylight is an issue); Building for Healthy Life statement (new housing); socio-economic impact assessment (larger commercial schemes).
issues.evidence: Local Validation Requirements table, 'Types of application' column.

issues.detail: 'Section 106 / Unilateral Undertaking heads of terms' is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The source requires it for 'All new residential development, including change of use to flats' through planning applications, so it belongs under Full and Outline residential applications, not prior approval. Grokbot appears to have matched the phrase 'change of use'.
issues.evidence: Trigger excerpt: 'All applications for new residential development ... including change of use to flats'.

issues.detail: The 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' row is actually the town centre Sequential Test and Impact Assessment for retail, leisure and office uses, so it is mislabelled. Its trigger also omits the thresholds: main town centre uses outside centres, with impact assessment above 900 sqm retail, 1,000 sqm offices and 2,500 sqm leisure. No flood sequential test item appears in this part of the source.
issues.evidence: Item 'Sequential test and impact assessment (Retail / leisure / office uses)'.

issues.detail: The Affordable Housing Statement trigger reads only 'See SPD 15 Appendix 1' and omits the thresholds given in the list: 15 or more dwellings in Housing Market Zones 1-4, and 11 or more in Zone 5.
issues.evidence: Affordable housing statement row, 'Types of application' column.

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are column dumps or fragments rather than triggers. 'Marketing / vacancy evidence' and 'Structural Survey' both quote a run of headers ('Structural survey Marketing statement OFFICIAL Policy background...'); the real triggers are demolition of heritage buildings, Assets of Community Value or pubs (marketing), and substantial demolition or works affecting heritage asset stability (structural). 'Floor plans / Elevations' quotes the street view elevations text. 'Roof plan' runs into the window details text. 'Heritage Statement' is 'of the Heritage Statement.' 'Telecommunications' is 'of the mast/equipment.' 'Waste / Refuse' is 'design of refuse storage areas.' (the trigger is all new development or change of use). Transport Assessment and Travel Plan run on into the noise text. Noise and Ecology give no trigger: noise applies near main roads or rail or to noise-sensitive uses near noise sources, and ecology to all new build except householder and minor extensions, plus works to buildings likely used by bats. 'Photographs' quotes another item; the real trigger is 3D images or photos as agreed for large developments.

The Environmental Statement excerpt runs into the national Fire Statement header, and the Fire Statement row reads only '/ notes Fire statement development.' The Fire Statement is a national requirement (buildings of 18m or 7 storeys or more with 2 or more dwellings), not a local item, and Grokbot's row gives no trigger.
issues.evidence: National Validation Requirements section: Fire statement.

issues.detail: Every general item is tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', and several application types wrongly show '(none)'. Householder is '(none)', yet the list applies the roof plan and floor plans to extensions, window details to all new or replacement windows, street view elevations to conservation areas, and the tree survey and heritage statement wherever relevant. Works to trees is '(none)', although the tree survey trigger includes 'applications to fell or lop protected trees'. The telecoms statement covers 'planning and prior approval applications', but it is not placed under prior approval. Under LBC, only the schedule of works is captured, not the Heritage statement.
issues.evidence: Tree survey row: '...applications to fell or lop protected trees'; Telecommunications statement: planning and prior approval applications.

issues.detail: The tab captured only two drawing-standard fragments ('The plan should include a north point.' and a street-view elevation fragment), so the tab does not reflect the 45-item local list. docs_read also includes 'Verification requirements for cover systems' (file 4436), which is contamination remediation guidance, not a validation document.
issues.evidence: tab_items; downloads page lists file 4436 as 'Verification requirements for cover systems'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Hull validation checklist (adopted 17 January 2023), but the date is recorded as 2023-01-01. The extraction misses about 15 of 45 local items. Several rows are mislabelled or misplaced: S106 heads of terms sits under prior approval, the retail sequential test is labelled as a flood test, and many triggers are column fragments without thresholds.
